sum: Starbucks Corporation SBUX reported mixed fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results on Oct. 29, with earnings surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 9.6%, while revenues missed the same by 1.4%. The company's "Back to Starbucks" efforts supported stronger sales leverage and lower costs, while the shift to a licensed business in China weighed on reported revenues.

Starbucks reported adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of 80 cents, up 54% from the prior-year quarter, while revenues of $9.14 billion declined 4.5% year over year. Global comparable sales increased 7.2%, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of growth. U.S. comparable sales rose 7.7%, supported by a 2.4% increase in transactions and a 5.2% rise in average ticket. North America revenues increased 6.3% to $7.33 billion. (Read more: Starbucks Q4 Earnings Beat Estimates on Sales Leverage, Revenues Miss)

For fiscal 2027, Starbucks expects North America comparable sales growth of approximately 4% and non-GAAP consolidated operating margin of 13.5-14%. Management projects adjusted EPS of $3.15-$3.25, representing nearly 18% growth at the midpoint, including a benefit of slightly more than 10 cents from an additional fiscal week.

Shares of Starbucks have gained 27.4% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Retail - Restaurants industry's fall of 1.6%. Industry peers Dutch Bros Inc. BROS and McDonald's Corporation MCD declined 44.9% and 10.3%, respectively, over the same period, as shown in the chart below.

With improving coffeehouse execution, growing loyalty engagement and cost efficiencies supporting its earnings recovery, does SBUX offer further upside following its strong share-price performance? Let’s assess.

Starbucks’ operating recovery broadened across North America in the fiscal fourth quarter, with more than 80% of company-operated coffeehouses reporting positive comparable sales, up from less than 50% a year earlier. Green Apron Service, Smart Queue refinements and improved operating routines supported throughput and service consistency. Daily deliveries reached nearly 90% of North America company-operated locations, improving product availability.
The company completed more than 1,700 North American coffeehouse upgrades in fiscal 2026, exceeding its target.

Starbucks gives workers stock grants, bonuses amid company turnaround effort
sum: Starbucks announced that nearly 200,000 employees worldwide are receiving new stock grants as the coffee giant rolls out additional rewards tied to company performance and customer tipping.

The Seattle-based company announced that eligible full- and part-time workers, whom Starbucks calls “partners,” received new Bean Stock grants on Nov. 11. The annual stock grants are part of a program that lets employees share in the company’s ownership.

About 130,000 employees also have stock grants from previous years vesting this month, according to a release from the company’s chief partner and chief operating officers. More than 2 million workers have received roughly $2.75 billion in pre-tax gains through the Bean Stock program since 1991.
More than 80% of eligible hourly employees at North American stores will receive a payout on Nov. 13 through its new “Best of Starbucks Reward” program, Starbucks reported.

The incentive program, announced earlier this year, lets eligible baristas and shift supervisors earn up to $300 per quarter when their stores meet certain sales, operational, and customer-service goals.

In addition to stock awards and bonuses, Starbucks reported that customers have tipped workers more than $22 million through expanded digital tipping options introduced in July. Tipping through those channels has more than doubled.
The expanded compensation programs are part of the company’s broader “Back to Starbucks” strategy, which aims to improve store performance and employee experience.

The transaction adds an insider-trading data point to a stock that has recently drawn attention from analysts. It does not by itself establish a change in Starbucks' operating outlook, but it gives investors another ownership signal to weigh alongside the company's turnaround effort.

Starbucks recently disclosed a quarterly dividend of 0.63 US dollars per share. The company plans to pay the dividend on Friday, November 27, while investors listed as shareholders on Friday, November 13, are scheduled to receive it. The ex-dividend date is also November 13.

The quarterly payment represents an annualized dividend of 2.52 US dollars per share, with a dividend yield of 2.3% according to The Cerbat Gem. E-Mart Shares Drop Over 7% Intraday After Earnings Disclosure… Impact of Starbucks’ Weak Performance
sum: E-Mart shares turned sharply lower during trading on the afternoon of the 11th. Analysts attribute the surge in sell orders to the confirmed weak third-quarter performance of SCK Company, its subsidiary that operates Starbucks.
At 2:07 p.m., E-Mart traded at 65,300 won on the Korea Exchange, down 5,500 won (7.77%) from the previous close. At one point during trading, the stock price fell as low as 63,700 won.
After opening higher, E-Mart shares fluctuated around flat levels throughout the morning before plunging simultaneously with the disclosure of its third-quarter preliminary earnings at 1:10 p.m.

On a consolidated basis, E-Mart reported third-quarter revenue of 7.7919 trillion won and an operating profit of 46.1 billion won. Revenue increased by 1.2% year-on-year, but operating profit decreased by 69.6%. The consensus estimate for operating profit compiled by FnGuide was 159.5 billion won.
On a standalone basis, the company posted revenue of 5.104 trillion won and an operating profit of 166 billion won, representing year-on-year increases of 11.1% and 3.3%, respectively.

However, the combined operating losses of its major consolidated subsidiaries reached 80.6 billion won. SCK Company recorded an operating loss of 45.3 billion won in the third quarter, turning to a deficit. Compared with the 60 billion won operating profit it generated in the same period last year, this represented the largest decline in operating profit among its subsidiaries.

sum: Starbucks (SBUX) Stock Rises 3.82% on Monday, Golden Cross Formed
Technical analysis of SBUX stock on November 9, 2026: price 109.44 USD, trend uptrend, RSI 66.9, support 92.00, resistance 109.70.

Starbucks shares closed at $109.44 on Monday, November 9, 2026, on the Nasdaq, up 3.82% from a prior close of $105.41. The stock is now 1.8% below its three-month high of $111.50. That is a long way from where the coffee chain stood a month ago: the shares have gained 18.58% over one month and 4.83% over five days.

The jump was about 1.3 times the stock's average daily range, so it was large but not unusual. What makes the session notable is what it did to the chart: a golden cross, a three-month-high test and a rising on-balance volume line all line up on one side.

A golden cross is a bullish pattern in which the short-term moving average climbs through the longer-term one. Here the 20-day simple moving average (SMA20) crossed above the 50-day (SMA50). The cross formed three sessions before the latest session, so it is recent but not brand new. The SMA20 sits at $101.83 and the SMA50 at $99.18, with the price well above both.
The 20-day average rose 3.54% over five days. That figure describes the average itself, not the share price, but it shows the recent buying has been persistent rather than a single spike.

As shown in the chart below, the price has pushed to the top of its short-term range. The 20-day resistance is $109.70, and the close of $109.44 sits at 99% of the range between support at $92.00 and that ceiling.

Starbucks stock gains as Q4 margins widen despite China revenue drag
sum: Starbucks reported stronger comparable sales and profitability for the fiscal fourth quarter ended September 27, 2026, while the transition of its China business to a licensed joint venture reduced consolidated revenue. The company said in its October 29 financial release that its Back to Starbucks plan supported a fifth consecutive quarter of global comparable-sales growth.

Global comparable coffeehouse sales rose 7.2 percent in the quarter. North America increased 7.9 percent, supported by a 2.7 percent rise in comparable transactions and a 5.0 percent increase in average ticket. U.S. comparable sales climbed 7.7 percent, while international comparable sales grew 0.9 percent as higher tickets only partly offset weaker transactions.

Consolidated revenue fell 4.5 percent to 9.14 billion US dollars. Starbucks attributed the decline primarily to the conversion of its China retail operations from company-operated stores to a licensed joint venture, which removed much of the retail revenue from consolidation. International revenue declined 36.9 percent to 1.31 billion US dollars, but segment operating income rose to 256.9 million US dollars and its margin widened to 19.7 percent.

Consolidated GAAP operating margin increased to 10.8 percent from 2.9 percent a year earlier, helped by lower restructuring costs and sales leverage. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 14.0 percent, while non-GAAP earnings per share rose 54 percent to 0.80 US dollars. The reported figures include the effects of restructuring and the China transaction; Starbucks separately presents adjusted measures for operating comparisons.

For fiscal 2027, management expects consolidated revenue to decline by approximately 1 percent, including approximately 700 million US dollars from a 53rd week and the China business-model change. The company targets North America comparable-sales growth of approximately 4.0 percent, a non-GAAP operating margin of 13.5 to 14.0 percent, non-GAAP earnings per share of 3.15 to 3.25 US dollars and approximately 1,200 net new coffeehouses.

Is Dutch Bros Stock a Buy as Shares Plunge?
sum: For the second time in two quarters, Dutch Bros (BROS -2.31%) shares collapsed following its earnings report, as investors fear that increasing competition is starting to eat into its growth. However, the company's overall same-store sales growth is still solid in a difficult consumer environment, and it continues to have one of the best expansion opportunities in the restaurant space.

The stock is now down more than 40% on the year, reversing the strong momentum the stock saw earlier in 2026. This looks like a golden opportunity to buy Dutch Bros in my view, as the stock's long-term underlying investment thesis remains unchanged.
Let's take a closer look at the coffee shop operator's third-quarter results and prospects and why I think it is a buy on this dip.

The biggest reason to own Dutch Bros is that it is one of the best expansion stories in the consumer space. The company opened 48 shops in Q3, of which 42 were company-opened, and plans to open at least 185 this year. It ended the quarter with 1,273 locations, of which 960 were company-owned shops. Meanwhile, it forecasted that it will open around 250 locations in 2027, which would be about 19% growth.

The company said it now has full visibility with its real estate pipeline to reach its goal of 2,029 shops in 2029. Its longer-term goal is to have 7,000 shops in the U.S., and it said it's being deliberate about how and where it grows, and it's not just simply about opening new locations and entering new states. In 2027, it plans to open most of its new shops in existing markets to benefit from increased density and to build brand awareness in these markets.

Dutch Bros shops typically have smaller footprints with two drive-thrus and no indoor seating, and are cost-efficient to build. This lets the company fund expansion fully with its operating cash flow. And while its shops are small, they generate a lot of revenue per location, with average unit volume (AUV) of more than $2.2 million. That helps the company get quick paybacks on new stores, increasing cash flow, and letting it funnel that back into new shops.
Dutch Bros also continues to deliver solid same-store sales. For Q3, comparable-store sales rose by 4.4%, as traffic increased by 0.4%.

Starbucks (SBUX) Stock Could Be 33% Overvalued As Growth Plans Expand
sum: Starbucks shares have climbed 27.2% over the past year, and with investors focused on expansion plans and profitability, the real issue is whether the current price is supported by the cash the business is expected to generate. The stock now trades around US$106, so the key lens is what its cash flows suggest about intrinsic value.
The 27.2% 1 year return puts real weight on the question of whether Starbucks' current valuation can be explained by its cash flow profile.
Management is leaning into global store growth and digital investments, which can reshape both the timing and level of future cash inflows as new locations and higher service efficiency reach scale.
For investors, the debate is whether Starbucks' recent share price strength is adequately backed by the cash flows implied by a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view of its intrinsic value.
To pressure test Starbucks' 27.2% 1 year return against similar cash flow stories, it helps to weigh it against other companies screened for 42 high quality undervalued stocks

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here uses Starbucks' projected free cash flows to judge what the current price implies. Latest twelve month free cash flow sits at about $2.8b, with the model assuming that this builds over time into higher annual cash generation by the late 2020s and early 2030s rather than shrinking.

On those cash flow forecasts, the DCF suggests an estimated intrinsic value that is substantially below the present share price of $106.16. Starbucks' push to add thousands of new outlets and sharpen digital ordering, highlighted in the recent "Back to Starbucks" growth plan, helps explain why the market is willing to pay a richer price than the cash flow model supports right now. NVDA Stock In For ‘Very, Very Fast’ Rally: Analysts Shrug Off Price-Hike Buzz Ahead Of Most-Watched Earnings Report
sum: Shares of Nvidia, Inc. (NVDA) rose nearly 1% in premarket trading on Tuesday, attempting to rebound from a seven-session rout as analysts argued that potential price increases for its newest AI systems should not derail demand and could strengthen an already bullish earnings setup.
NVDA stock fell 3% on Monday but remains up 4% for August, putting it on track for its strongest monthly performance since May.

Nvidia could reportedly raise prices for its Blackwell and Rubin systems as soaring memory costs push up production expenses. However, Raymond James analyst Simon Leopold said that a potential 15% increase would make sense given the amount of high-bandwidth memory packed into the platforms. “15% really doesn’t seem all that demanding,” Leopold said, adding that an even larger increase is possible.

Each Blackwell and Rubin GPU is paired with eight HBM stacks, each containing 12 layers of DRAM. Nvidia has also spent years locking in memory supplies through long-term agreements with multiple suppliers, potentially cushioning the effect of rising costs.

Still, Leopold cautioned that higher list prices may not translate directly into higher prices for major customers. “The public prices may go up by 15%, but that doesn’t mean contracted prices are reflecting that same amount,” he said.

Wall Street is bracing for another enormous quarter from Nvidia on Wednesday. Fiscal.ai projects revenue of $91.48 billion, more than double the year-earlier figure, with adjusted earnings of $2.07 per share and EBITDA of $61.83 billion.

Koyfin’s estimates are slightly higher at $92.07 billion in revenue, $2.09 in adjusted earnings and $61.99 billion in EBITDA. This would represent sequential growth of 13% in revenue and EBITDA and 12% in earnings.

sum: McDonald's Corporation’s MCD shares have declined 22.9% over the past six months, underperforming the restaurant industry, which fell 16.7%, and the S&P 500, which gained 10.8%. The sell-off reflects concerns about slowing U.S. sales momentum, inconsistent execution of value offerings, weaker-than-expected marketing results and a challenging consumer environment.

McDonald's stock has faced several headwinds over the past six months. First, the U.S. business has struggled to generate stronger comparable sales growth amid a challenging consumer environment. Second, the company's value-menu strategy did not deliver the expected increase in customer traffic. Third, operational inefficiencies and underwhelming marketing campaigns weakened customer engagement. Concerns about development costs and a slower restaurant expansion timeline have added to the challenges.

These issues were evident in the second quarter of 2026, when global comparable sales increased just 1.3%, while U.S. comparable sales grew 0.8%. Management acknowledged that execution in the United States fell short of expectations.
In the same time frame, McDonald’s has underperformed restaurant peers including Starbucks Corporation SBUX, Yum! Brands, Inc. YUM and Chipotle Mexican Grill, Inc. CMG.

McDonald's introduced its Every Day Affordable Price menu in April 2026, offering 10 items priced below $3. However, the initiative failed to generate the expected incremental sales because of inconsistent execution and limited consumer awareness. Only about 60-65% of the U.S. restaurant system followed the recommended pricing structure.

The company also reduced digital offers and discontinued its Buy One, Add One for $1 promotion to offset the cost of its value initiatives. These changes disappointed some frequent customers. Management attributed roughly two-thirds of the U.S. customer traffic shortfall against its expectations to these value-related execution issues.

Marketing performance added to the pressure. McDonald's U.S. business faced a difficult comparison with the previous year's successful Minecraft campaign, while its FIFA campaign in June generated less business than expected. These shortcomings suggest that the company needs to improve its promotional strategy to bring customers back more consistently.

items.t: Best Dividend Stocks to Hold in 2026—Microsoft, Starbucks or American Express?
sum: Dividend stocks offer investors a way to balance growth with stability amidst AI-driven market volatility. Companies with resilient cash flows and prudent capital allocation can provide reliable income, irrespective of stock price movements. Key considerations for selecting dividend stocks include consistent earnings, robust Free Cash Flow, and strong balance sheets. Industries like Utilities, Energy, and Consumer Staples traditionally offer stable dividends. While dividend growth stocks may offer lower initial yields, they can provide superior total returns over time, especially when dividends are reinvested. Investors must also assess risks such as potential dividend cuts and tax implications.

TradingKey - As artificial intelligence transforms industries and adds to the volatility of markets, investors want names that can help smooth that out without sacrificing growth. The best dividend stocks can help with that objective by combining resilient cash flows with prudent capital allocation.

Dividend stocks are shares of companies that pay out a portion of their earnings to shareholders on a regular basis. While growth stocks tend to plow the majority of their earnings back into the company, dividend-payers typically balance rewarding investors today with funding future growth.

A dividend is the portion of the earnings of the company which it distributes among its shareholders, and it is generally paid quarterly. Dividend Yield is the annual dividend per share divided by the share price, so it provides an easy way to see how much income you get for every dollar invested. But a more important figure than the headline yield is a company’s capacity to pay that dividend for longer and longer periods of time. That means consistent earnings, robust Free Cash Flow, and a balance sheet that can weather the storms of multiple economic cycles, if need be, to make it through to the other side.

AI has injected a potent growth narrative into markets, but it has also exacerbated dispersion between winners and laggards. There are times when exuberance pushes valuations up and any stumbling in adoption, regulation, or capital expenditure causes massive selloffs. In that regard, dividend stocks can help steady the ship.

items.t: Coffee Stock Battle: Starbucks (SBUX), Dutch Bros (BROS), and Luckin (LKNCY)
sum: Tea is still big in Asia, but one of the most interesting trends is the explosion of alternatives from black coffee to flavored and blended drinks incorporating coffee. The biggest laboratory for this is in a country with 1.3 billion potential coffee drinkers - China.
China now has more coffee shops than the United States, according to the World Coffee Portal, a market research firm. The market grew 25% from 2018 to 2023, according to Bain & Company estimates.

Coffee king Starbucks (SBUX) has struggled in both China and the U.S. lately, but we can see some seeds of a turnaround led by Brian Niccol, who took the CEO role in September 2024, after previously leading Chipotle and Taco Bell. Through a combination of closing unproductive coffeehouses, new products, and incentives, you can see a turnaround happening.

In the first quarter of fiscal 2026, Starbucks reported a global comparable store sales increase of 4% year over year, with North America comparable store sales up 4%. The gains were driven by higher transaction volumes and higher average ticket size. This is promising.

Starbucks is also seeking to lower exposure in China as it appears that consumers are less interested in foreign brands, are more cost-conscious and often enticed by local rivals that are popping up on corners all around the country offering something a little different.

A smaller disruptive chain called Dutch Bros (BROS) has demonstrated some impressive growth over the last few years. An operator and franchisor of drive-thru coffee stores, the company has rapidly expanded its stable of stores. It is more than just coffee and offers a plethora of drinks aimed at younger customers.

It has expanded rapidly, growing to 1,100 locations, with plans to open 2,029 by 2029 and 7,000 in the U.S. over the long term. Dutch Bros has introduced mobile buy-ahead ordering, which has been helping drive same-store sales as well as hot food items. The company turned profitable two years ago and in 2025 reported $29.2 million in net income, up from $6.4 million in the year-before period.

items.t: Starbucks Shares Are Up 13.7% Year-to-Date: Is It a Buy?
sum: Shares of international coffeehouse giant Starbucks (SBUX +3.82%) are up 13.7% in 2026 so far, as Wall Street reacted favorably to the company's Q4 2025 earnings report. From growing same-store sales to a 5% bump in global revenue and the opening of 128 net new coffeehouses around the world, it was the most triumphant earnings report since former Chipotle Mexican Grill CEO Brian Niccol took the helm of Starbucks in September 2024.

I own shares in Starbucks, but despite the recent positive news, I won't be adding to my position. For all of the hopeful statistics, one number in the company's fundamentals is a dealbreaker. A successful turnaround could change things, but for now, there's still work to be done.
Here's what I'm watching to see if Starbucks can return to its glory days.

While the share price is up this year, it's down about 24% from its all-time high of $126 per share in July 2021. Back then, Starbucks had just reported Q3 2021 earnings. Looking back, it's striking how much ground it's lost in the 4.5 years since.

At the time, Starbucks had just reported two-year U.S. revenue growth of 16% since Q3 2019, a figure which wouldn't have been skewed by the pandemic. Two-year same-store sales growth in the U.S. was 10%, while the company added over a million active Starbucks Rewards members that quarter, bringing its total to 24 million active members. In China, two-year revenue growth had surged 45%. Net earnings came in at $1.15 billion.

But last quarter, the company reported just $293.3 in net income for the most recent quarter, a 75% decrease from quarterly net income at the stock's all-time high. Granted, much of this collapse is explained by Starbucks' recent deal to turn its China locations into a joint venture with Boyu Capital, in which the latter is taking an up to 60% interest in its retail operations.

But this doesn't strike me as much of a silver lining. One of the biggest reasons to be bullish on Starbucks used to be that it was poised to tap into the Chinese market, where up to 400 million people could soon be joining the middle-income population.

Investors Are Piling Into This Stock That's Up 28,000% Since Its IPO. Can It Soar in 2026?
sum: Coffee shop leader Starbucks (SBUX -0.31%) has disappointed investors over the past few years, but after cycling through four CEOs over the past four years, it might finally be turning around.

Shareholders have had high hopes for star CEO Brian Niccol, who joined the company just over a year ago, and his action plan looks like it might be starting to bear fruit. Is the stock a buy for 2026?

Starbucks is a massive coffee shop chain, with more than 41,000 stores worldwide. It's not easy to steer an organization that big and that entrenched in legacy systems, and the company has fallen behind in several important ways as global trends change. Wait times have been sluggish, prices are high, and the company's "third place" designation appeared outdated in the era of digitization.

Niccol is actually leaning into the third-place status, but he's revamping the company's image, processes, and equipment to make it relevant to today's customer. The company has been more deliberate with promotions, has changed its marketing story, and has put a lot of effort into improving its throughput to get beverages into customers' hands quickly without compromising on quality.

Starbucks may finally be demonstrating progress. In the 2026 fiscal first quarter (ended Dec. 28), revenue increased 6% year over year to $9.9 billion, while comparable sales were up 4% globally. Adjusted earnings per share declined 19% to $0.56. Niccol is heavily investing in the improvement strategy, which weighed on the bottom line, but he anticipates it will eventually lead to better margins and increased profitability when the investments pay off.
Starbucks has been an incredible market winner over time, gaining almost 28,000% since its debut on the stock market, and more than 37,000% when you include dividends.
Starbucks' dividend yields about 2.6% at the current price, and the company has raised it annually for the past 15 years.

items.t: From Starbucks to Burger King: Western food giants are selling large stakes to Chinese private equity funds
sum: - Chinese private equity firms tend to move fast, revamping menus, adjusting prices and scaling rapidly, including into lower-tier cities.
- Their readiness to shake up management and stronger ties to local suppliers, distributors, landlords and regulators also make divesting more appealing.
- China subsidiaries of multinational brands have also become prized targets for financial sponsors eager to deploy idle capital after years of tepid dealmaking.

Starbucks and Burger King are betting big on a partnership model that's gaining traction in China: selling majority stakes to local private equity firms as the battle for market share rages on. Foreign food-and-beverage chains once thrived in China without adapting much — premium Western products practically sold themselves. Today, decisions made from distant headquarters no longer cut it. Chinese private equity firms tend to move fast, revamping menus, adjusting prices and scaling rapidly, including into lower-tier cities. "Their involvement enables the business to operate at 'China speed,'" said Kei Hasegawa, partner at consulting firm YCP. Starbucks is selling a 60% stake in its China unit to Boyu Capital in a $4 billion deal, projecting its value will more than triple over the next decade, including licensing fees to the Seattle-based giant. CPE Capital is investing $350 million in Burger King's China operations, taking an 83% stake. Both joint ventures are pending regulatory approval in China and expected to complete next year. This month, Hong Kong-headquartered IDG Capital acquired a controlling stake in French yogurt brand Yoplait's China business in a deal valuing the unit at about $250 million . That's just a taste of things to come. General Mills is reportedly considering selling its Haagen-Dasz stores in China. Swedish oat milk brand Oatly Group AB has also been reportedly exploring divesting its China business . Western brands have seen their fortunes shift as homegrown players surge ahead with competitive pricing, smart digital strategies and a sharper read on local consumer preferences. Luckin Coffee overtook Starbucks in both sales and store count in 2023 . Restaurant Brands International has struggled with Burger King in China, with average per-store sales ranking the lowest among its major markets.

Worst CEOs Of The Year: Brian Niccol Of Starbucks
sum: Today, we start a list of the worst CEOs in America. There will be an all-time winner later in the year. The way these CEOs are picked stems from major strategy stumbles. It also included a series of decisions we made that affect three groups. These are shareholders, customers, and employees. Some of these CEOs are fairly new to the public corporations they run. Others have had their jobs for years.
(NASDAQ: SBUX | SBUX Price Prediction) CEO Brian Niccol is first on the list.
Starbucks Corp.’s share price suggests the company’s best year is well behind it, based on its performance over the last five years. The stock is down 16% while the S&P 500 is up 84%.

The coffee store company has had a series of chief executives over the period. Kevin Johnson, Howard Schultz, Laxman Narasimhan, and Brian Niccol have all held the job. Schultz has had the job twice recently. He did not found the company, but his success in its early days made him close to one. His net worth has been pegged at $3 billion.

Niccol is the board’s latest CEO experiment. After a little more than a year, it has already failed, particularly for those who look at the stock price. In March, it topped $117. Today, it trades at $83. Based on three quarters of earnings and a set of announcements about planned improvements, investors have lost whatever patience they had.

Niccol was expected to be a turnaround artist due to his track record at Taco Bell and Chipotle (NYSE: CMG). His lack of success at Starbucks has included a line of statements primarily about how Starbucks might return to its roots as a community coffeehouse where baristas are friendly and well-dressed. When people order, their orders will come fast, his plan said. That is because he has streamlined the menus. The baristas will also remember people’s names and sometimes write them on cups

What does Niccol have to show for his plans? He dumped Starbucks operations in China, which was supposed to be its fastest-growing market and eventually, perhaps, its largest. Starbucks sold 40% of its China operations for $4 billion, plus brand licensing and some upside. The buyer was Boyu Capital, which, while local, does not appear to have deep roots in the coffee shop business.

Starbucks apologizes after Bearista cup launch sparks chaos: 'Exceeded even our biggest expectations'
sum: Starbucks has issued an apology to customers after the release of its limited-edition teddy bear–shaped holiday cup sparked chaos.
The Seattle-based coffee giant launched its 2025 holiday menu and merchandise on Thursday, including the Glass Starbucks Bearista Cold Cup, which retails for $29.95.
The collectible cup — shaped like a bear and topped with a green beanie lid — went viral online and sold out quickly, leaving fans scrambling to get their hands on one.

"The excitement for our merchandise exceeded even our biggest expectations and, despite shipping more Bearista cups to coffeehouses than almost any other merchandise item this holiday season, the Bearista cup and some other items sold out fast," a Starbucks spokesperson told FOX Business in an email.
The spokesperson added, "We understand many customers were excited about the Bearista cup and apologize for the disappointment this may have caused."

In Harris County, Texas, law enforcement was reportedly called to a Starbucks after customers began fighting inside the store and refused to leave, local outlet KHOU 11 reported, citing Harris County Precinct 4.
The dispute reportedly started over the popular Bearista cups.

items.t: Starbucks' union workers plan strike next week on Red Cup Day unless company agrees to contract
sum: Starbucks' union members have voted to strike at the company's U.S. stores next week unless it finalizes a contract agreement, the union said Wednesday.

The strike would begin on Nov. 13, which is the day Starbucks plans to distribute free, reusable red cups. Red Cup Day, a Starbucks tradition since 2018, is typically one of the company's busiest days of the year.

Starbucks Workers United, the union organizing baristas, didn't say how many stores would be impacted. But it said workers in at least 25 cities planned to strike and more locations could be added if the union doesn't see "substantial progress" toward finalizing a contract.

Around 550 of Starbucks' 10,000 company-operated U.S. stores are currently unionized. More stores have voted to unionize since 2021, but Starbucks closed 59 unionized stores in September as part of a larger restructuring.

The union and the company have yet to agree to a labor contract. In December 2023, Starbucks vowed to finalize an agreement by the end of 2024. But the company ousted Laxman Narasimhan, the CEO who made that promise, last fall. The union said progress has stalled under Brian Niccol, the company's new chairman and CEO.
Starbucks said Wednesday that it's disappointed the union plans to strike instead of returning to the bargaining table.

"Any agreement needs to reflect the reality that Starbucks already offers the best job in retail, including more than $30 an hour on average in pay and benefits for hourly partners," Starbucks spokeswoman Jaci Anderson said Wednesday.
